(Memphis, Tennessee) | college = [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] (2015–2016) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] All-American (2015) * [[Nike Hoop Summit]] (2015) * First-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] (2015) }} '''Skal Labissière''' ({{IPA-fr|labissjɛʁ}}; born March 18, 1996) is a Haitian [[basketball]] player who most recently played for the [[2015–16 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky Wildcats]].[http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Skal-Labissiere-71664/ DraftExpress: Skal Labissiere]{{cite web|url=http://lenouvelliste.com/lenouvelliste/article/143806/Skal-Labissiere-draft-1-NBA-100-haitien |title=Skal Labissière, draft #1 NBA 100 % haïtien |editor=Press |publisher=Le Nouvelliste |date=20 April 2015 |accessdate=4 June 2015}} {{fr icon}} ==Early years== Labissière was born in [[Port-au-Prince]], Haiti. His basketball career began at the [[Collège Canado-Haïtien]], a junior-senior high school in Port-au-Prince, which participated in school championships organized by the {{not a typo|Comité Interscolaire de Basket-ball Amateur}} (CIBA), and the {{not a typo|Association de Basket-ball Interscolaire}} (ASI). During the [[2010 Haiti earthquake]], his family's home collapsed with Labissière, his mother and his brother inside. All three survived but were trapped under the debris for the next three hours. Skal's legs were trapped, causing them to go numb and he was unable to walk for a few weeks after. A few months after the earthquake, Labissière moved to the [[United States]] in Memphis, Tennessee to live with Gerald Hamilton who ran the Reach Your Dream Foundation, which brought international prospects to the United States.[http://espn.go.com/high-school/boys-basketball/story/_/id/7448728/skal-labissiere-survived-2010-haiti-earthquake Rise Above: Skal Labissiere]{{cite web|url=http://www.kentucky.com/2013/01/31/2498350/kentucky-target-labissiere-a-walking.html |title=Kentucky target Labissiere a walking, shooting 'miracle' |editor=Roberts, Ben |date=31 January 2013 |accessdate=25 March 2015}}[http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/story/19614399/after-surviving-haitis-quake-labissiere-out-to-make-most-of-his-second-chance After surviving Haiti's quake, Labissiere out to make most of his second chance] ==High school career== Labissière attended [[Evangelical Christian School]] in Memphis and started to play varsity basketball as an eighth-grader. When he had first arrived, Labissière spoke little English and required a [[French language|French]] interpreter in all of his classes. After three to four months, he didn't need the help and became fluent. In 2014, he left the school his senior year and enrolled at [[Lausanne Collegiate School]], also located in Memphis,[http://www.commercialappeal.com/sports/high-school/skal-labissiere-enrolls-at-lausanne-wont-play-basketball-for-lynx_20825363 Skal Labissiere enrolls at Lausanne, but apparently won't play basketball, AD says] but because of the move he was ruled by [[Tennessee Secondary School Athletic Association|TSSAA]] as ineligible to play basketball at Lausanne for the season. So instead, Labissière played for Gerald Hamilton's Reach Your Dream Prep Academy team, where he averaged 26 points, 12 rebounds and 4.5 blocks per UK's coach [[John Calipari]], offered Labissière a scholarship before any other 2015 prospect, comparing him to [[Anthony Davis (basketball)|Anthony Davis]]. Before entering the 2015-16 season, Labissière was considered to be one of the top candidates of being the #1 selection for the [[2016 NBA Draft]]. Despite holding such strong merit at the time, Labissière would not live up to the hype he put up during his only season at Kentucky, which included him being relegated to bench duties throughout half of their entire season. ===College statistics=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2015–16]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2015–16 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] | 36 || 18 || 15.8 || .516 || .000 || .661 || 3.1 || .3 || .3 || .8 || 6.6 |- {{S-end}} ==Professional career== Labissière was one of 59 different college/postgraduate students to enter the [[2016 NBA Draft]].
